_about: Key places on the map: 3 to 5 per region, only places an official source names, each line one idea, all backed by the cites (owner card 18 Oct 2026, style B name chips). Shown while one of the listed places is selected. Positions are OpenStreetMap points (data/SOURCES.md, Map flags).

flags.name: Haro
lines: A French firm in its station quarter hired a champagne maker from Reims in 1890.

flags.name: Sierra de Cantabria
lines: The mountains on the northern side.
They shelter Rioja Alta, and Rioja Alavesa even more.

flags.name: Ebro
lines: The vineyards lie on both banks of the river.
Alluvial soils near the rivers make up half the land.

flags.name: Alfaro
lines: Rioja's easternmost town, 100 km from Haro.

flags.name: Jerez de la Frontera
lines: One of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.

flags.name: Sanlúcar de Barrameda
lines: One of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.
Manzanilla has its own DO named after it.

flags.name: El Puerto de Santa María
lines: The third of the three towns where Sherry must be aged.

flags.name: Guadalete
lines: The river is the southern edge of the area where Sherry is aged.

flags.name: Chipiona
lines: Moscatel may also be aged here, and in Chiclana.
